StorytellerDef.label: The Long Road
StorytellerDef.description:
The world calls the colony out. Fewer raids come to the gate, about three quarters of the classic pace, and more of the story waits in the region: letters asking for help, favours called in, camps on the land, missions and quests, travellers on the road. Ambushes and chance meetings follow the colony's caravans more than its walls.

For a game of journeys and the region map.

It leans toward these, never away from anything: every kind of event can still come.

StorytellerDef.label: Neighbours
StorytellerDef.description:
The peoples around are the story. Raids come a little less often than the classic pace, and most come from a people with a reason: one the colony wronged, an old enemy. Peoples call in their favours and ask the colony into their quarrels, write and visit more, and a people the colony helped is likelier to send fighters when it is attacked.

For a game of diplomacy, debts and old grudges.

It leans toward these, never away from anything: every kind of event can still come.

StorytellerDef.label: The Turning Year
StorytellerDef.description:
The calendar decides. Quiet springs, with sickness coming with the thaw; growing summers of heat waves and blight; trade and camps in autumn, when the harvest is in; then a hard winter, its cold snaps and the hungry raids of late winter. Every year has the same shape and different contents, so the colony can plan for its seasons. Over a year the threats and the sickness come about as often as the classic pace.

For a game of fields, stores and the colony's calendar.

It leans toward these, never away from anything: every kind of event can still come.

StorytellerDef.label: What You Sow
StorytellerDef.description:
The colony's deeds decide, as the peoples remember them. Cruelty draws raiders with a grievance at the classic pace, and the roads thin: a quarter of the traders, visitors and friends in a fight still come. Kindness spares the colony a third of the raids and brings traders, visitors and friends at the gate in a fight. Nothing is told: the world simply answers, and its peoples remember longer.

For a game where how the colony treats others matters.

It leans toward these, never away from anything: every kind of event can still come.

StorytellerDef.label: Old Powers
StorytellerDef.description:
The world feels watched. Raids come about three quarters as often as the classic pace, and stranger things come in their place: psychic drones, maddened herds, things in the earth, and the void where its powers are awake. Nights are full of omens, eclipses and auroras; pilgrims and seers are more often on the road, the land and the sky stir more, and the region's word turns to strange skies.

For a game of omens and the unknown.

It leans toward these, never away from anything: every kind of event can still come.

StorytellerDef.label: Lean Years
StorytellerDef.description:
Scarcity is the enemy, not raiders. Raids come about two thirds as often as the classic pace, but blights, cold snaps, heat waves and storms come often, traders are few and camps come seldom, and the region's word is of famine, drought and hard winters. The colony must feed and keep everyone through years that test it.

For a game of fields, stores and keeping everyone fed.

It leans toward these, never away from anything: every kind of event can still come.

StorytellerDef.label: Rise and Fall
StorytellerDef.description:
Long arcs of about two years. First a year of growth and plenty: few raids, traders, visitors and camps. Then the region's word of a great trouble, a war among the peoples, a plague, a famine, a hard winter or a darkness in the sky, and a season later the trouble itself: the war's raids, the plague's sickness, the famine's blights, the winter's cold. Then the rebuilding, quiet, with friends at hand, and the next arc. Over an arc the threats and the sickness come about as often as the classic pace.

For a game of long stories with an ending to each.

It leans toward these, never away from anything: every kind of event can still come.

StorytellerDef.label: Crossroads
StorytellerDef.description:
The colony as a market on a road through the land. Traders come about twice as often, orbital traders too, with visitors, travellers and camps of merchants, and debts and favours between the colony and its neighbours. Raiders are drawn by its wealth: a poor colony sees about half the classic pace of raids, a rich one the classic pace, and some raids come from rivals with a grudge. The region's word is of fairs, trade, roads and their tolls.

For a game of trade and wealth.

It leans toward these, never away from anything: every kind of event can still come.
